bibliographic.title: The Ethics of ChatGPT in Medicine and Healthcare: A Systematic Review on Large Language Models (LLMs)
bibliographic.citation_apa: Haltaufderheide, J., & Ranisch, R. (unclear). The ethics of ChatGPT in medicine and healthcare: A systematic review on large language models (LLMs) [Preprint version]. University of Potsdam.

methodology.method_family: systematic review with modified rapid review and meta-aggregative synthesis
methodology.sample_description: Electronic databases and preprint servers searched; records screened and extracted; methodological quality assessed with hybrid approach; subset synthesized meta-aggregatively
methodology.sample_size: 796 records identified; 53 records included in meta-aggregative synthesis
methodology.technology_context: Large Language Models (LLMs), including ChatGPT, in clinical, educational, and research healthcare applications

eligibility.decision_rationale: The study is a systematic review mapping ethical issues and application fields of LLMs in medicine and healthcare, with recurrent themes of fairness, bias, transparency, privacy, harm, and human oversight. It provides foundational ethical context for regulated LLM use but the supplied text does not focus on conversational governance mechanisms such as guardrails, observability, audit logs, tracing, or operational compliance controls.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only front matter and partial methods sources are supplied; full screening criteria, extraction protocol, quality appraisal details, and limitations require full-text verification.

appraisal.notes: Abstract reports a comprehensive search (796 records), modified rapid review screening/extraction, hybrid quality assessment, and meta-aggregative synthesis of 53 records. Database list is partially visible; limitations and full appraisal protocol are not shown in the provided excerpts.

cerqual.explanation: Findings are coherently summarized from a sizable screened sample and a defined synthesis subset, but the modified rapid review design and incomplete visibility of methods in the supplied text limit confidence for operational governance claims.

coding.theme: Ethical governance of LLMs in medicine and healthcare
coding.subtheme: Human oversight and acceptable thresholds across diverse healthcare use cases
concepts: necessity and justification of experimental use

synthesis.main_claim: LLM use in medicine and healthcare spans four application fields in an exploratory phase, offering benefits in data analysis, personalized information, and decision support, while recurrent ethical concerns include fairness, bias, transparency, privacy, and harmful misinformation.
synthesis.contribution: Provides a systematic map of practical LLM applications and connected ethical issues in healthcare, and reframes ethical guidance toward defining acceptable human oversight across settings with varying harm potential and performance thresholds.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as foundational contextual evidence on ethical risks, human oversight, transparency, bias, and privacy for LLMs in regulated healthcare; not primary evidence for operational conversational governance mechanisms.
